Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

respect noun and verb

esteem for someone

also respect for, show respect, out of respect, respect your elders, look up to, esteem, respectful

classical

Cic. Off. 1.122: est igitur adulēscentis majōrēs nātū verērī
Cic. Planc. 29: quem verētur ut deum

vereor, verērī, veritus sum

verb, second conjugation, deponent, with the accusative

respect, revere (a person); also fear

Lewis & Short: “to feel awe of, to reverence, revere, respect; to fear” (milder than metuō); frequent in Cicero, while Caesar, Livy and Sallust use only the participle veritus.

Other words

  • observō, observāre, observāvī, observātum — pay respect to, honour (a person)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.78.1: mēque praeter cēterōs et colit et observat et dīligit; Traupman 157

    Often paired with colō, honour: colere et observāre. For keeping to a rule, see respect (keep to).

  • observantia, observantiae f. — respect, the deference shown to elders and superiors

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Inv. 2.66: observantiam, per quam aetāte aut sapientiā aut honōre aut aliquā dignitāte antecēdentēs verēmur et colimus; Cic. Fam. 12.27.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • reverentia, reverentiae f. — respect, reverence

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.99: adhibenda est igitur quaedam reverentia adversus hominēs; Juv. 14.47: maxima dēbētur puerō reverentia (Lewis & Short)

    Rare until after the Augustan age (Lewis & Short); Juvenal’s line is the famous one: the greatest respect is owed to a child.

  • honōris causā — out of respect

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 6: L. Sullā, quem honōris causā nōminō

    The courtesy with which an orator names a great man: “whom I mention with all respect”. Lewis & Short: “out of respect, in order to show honor”.

  • observāns, observantis — respectful, attentive

    also used · classical · Traupman 157

Examples

  • Est igitur adulēscentis majōrēs nātū verērī exque iīs dēligere optimōs et probātissimōs, quōrum cōnsiliō atque auctōritāte nītātur

    It is the part of a young man, then, to respect his elders and to choose from among them the best and most approved, on whose advice and authority he may relyCic. Off. 1.122

  • summa in hospitēs līberālitās et observantia, mēque praeter cēterōs et colit et observat et dīligit

    the greatest generosity and courtesy towards guests; and he honours, respects and loves me more than anyoneCic. Fam. 13.78.1

  • adhibenda est igitur quaedam reverentia adversus hominēs et optimī cujusque et reliquōrum

    we must therefore show a certain respect towards people, both the best of them and all the restCic. Off. 1.99

See also respect, respect, consider, obedient.
